detail.longDescription: In the documentation for the YouTube IFrame API , the optional origin parameter is described: This parameter provides an extra security measure for the IFrame API and is only supported for IFrame embeds. If you are using the IFrame API, which means you are setting the enablejsapi parameter value to 1 , you should always specify your domain as the origin parameter value. While origin is optional, including it protects against malicious third-party JavaScript being injected into your page and hijacking control of your YouTube player. What types of hijacking could occur if origin isn't used? Would an attacker only be able to perform YouTube player-specific actions such as loading a different video, pausing, etc., or would they be able to engage beyond the YouTube player?
